execution_rule: Executable trace specifications awaiting an ACL2 owner/Store and native host runner. The future runner must reopen at each named cut and observe both fn's durable position and the consumer database. No current caller implements these actions, so none of these traces has executed.

fixtures.store_a: history HA, incarnation IA, administrator A
fixtures.store_b: history HB, incarnation IB, administrator B, same endpoint in replacement traces
fixtures.report_r: signed immutable source SR, Message-ID MR, application operation OR, dregg receipt DR
fixtures.reply_q: signed immutable source SQ, Message-ID MQ, correlation (OR, SR)
fixtures.view_1: initial query group agent.reports and principal agent-b policy; E2-06 initially hides R
fixtures.view_2: in E2-06, older hidden R becomes visible to agent-b

traces.name: sleep, filtered prefix and empty page
actions: commit nonarticle record 1 and hidden article 2 in HB/IB
register B under view 1
poll with scan limit 2; observe empty page and continuation at 2
commit R at record 3 while B sleeps
reopen fn
poll from continuation; commit B inbox R and Q outbox atomically
ack scanned prefix
reopen fn and B database
expect: no ack from either poll alone
empty page can advance through record 2 without exposing its identity
after reopen B has one R verdict and immutable Q; fn B position is 3
A's independent position remains unchanged
cuts: after B transaction before fn ack

traces.name: two consumers, one report
actions: register B and C on HB/IB
commit R
poll R as B and C
B commits inbox/outbox and acks
reopen fn and both databases
C polls its original cursor and commits independently
expect: B's recorded position advances without moving C's
each consumer has one local transition
no fn retention release is inferred
cuts: after B ack before C transaction

traces.name: duplicate transport and application operation conflict
actions: accept R on B via BP attempt X
receive duplicate R under attempt Y
deliver application retry R2 with new Message-ID and the same operation ID but different signed source
poll and atomically check B's unique (application-id, operation-id) index while storing both source-inclusive inbox records
reopen both stores
expect: R has one fn article/charge under the existing identity rule
X and Y remain distinguishable transport evidence
B makes one transition for OR and retains R2 as conflicting application evidence through its distinct inbox source key
unique operation index prevents a second transition and Q in outbox is byte-identical across replays
cuts: after B transaction commit before fn ack

traces.name: uncertain consumer transaction and uncertain ack
actions: poll R
kill B at the inbox/outbox transaction publication cut
reopen B database and query provenance inbox key, unique operation index and Q outbox key
complete transaction if absent or reuse exact Q if present
send ack and kill fn at the ack publication cut
reopen fn and query position
repeat the same ack only if position stayed old
expect: B has either neither record or both after its cut, never half a pair
after settlement B has one transition and one Q
fn position is old or advanced after its cut and never invented from socket output
repeat ack is idempotent

traces.name: endpoint replacement and restore fork
actions: B acks R in HB/IB
replace the endpoint with a copied store HB/IB2 whose local article numbers repeat
offer the old cursor and attempt ack
reopen replacement fn
explicitly rebase B under HB/IB2 and scan from zero
expect: old cursor is refused wrong-store/rebase-required without mutation
old HB/IB ack does not appear as HB/IB2 progress
R is offered again and B applies its explicit provenance/dedup policy

traces.name: authorization view makes old report visible
actions: commit hidden R at record 1 and visible Q at record 2
B scans and acks through record 2 under view 1
change effective read policy to view 2
attempt old cursor poll and ack
rebase and scan from zero
reopen fn and B database
expect: old view cursor is refused without advancing
new scan offers R despite its record position below the former ack
B's unique operation index deduplicates any repeated Q
old-view page contents and errors disclose no hidden source or article identity; the public-profile cursor may expose a committed-record position

traces.name: scope mismatch and bounded registration
actions: register B under query reports
offer B token as C and under query replies
offer a malformed or unknown-version token
fill the configured consumer table
attempt one more register
reopen fn
expect: all wrong-scope/token requests refuse before ack mutation under the authenticated caller
the full table refuses before a durable registration promise
existing positions survive reopen
bounded decode work and no denied article identity in refusals; no cursor-position privacy claim

traces.name: retention gap and independent page budgets
actions: commit visible R, then reclaim its article bytes under the existing retention decision before B polls
poll across R
restore the article from authorized evidence or declare an explicit application waiver
commit one article larger than the configured page-byte limit
poll across that article and reopen fn
expect: reclaimed visible R yields unavailable at its record position and no continuation past it
neither poll nor ack implies R was processed
an oversized single article yields bounded refusal without a cursor past it
scan, item, byte, token and registration limits are checked independently

traces.name: unregister and reuse consumer ID with delayed old ack
actions: register C under HB/IB, query reports and view 1; record epoch EC1
poll R and hold the resulting cursor without ack
durably unregister C and reopen fn
register C again under the same principal, query and view; record fresh epoch EC2
send the delayed EC1 ack as authenticated C
poll and ack R with EC2 cursor
reopen fn
expect: EC2 differs from EC1 despite identical consumer ID, query and view
delayed EC1 ack is refused before mutation
C's new position remains zero until EC2 ack commits
after reopen C's epoch and position match EC2, with no wall-clock-derived epoch
cuts: after second register publication before reply

traces.name: separate administrators, sleeping reply and uncertain post
actions: A commits R with exact-source hybrid authorship and dregg receipt DR
trusted peer transports R to B's separate Store while B sleeps
B verifies authorship and independently verifies DR
B commits inbox R with Q outbox and acks
B posts Q and loses final reply
lookup MQ and compare exact SQ before any retry
A wakes, verifies Q correlation to OR and SR, then commits its own inbox transaction
expect: HA/IA and HB/IB have independent numbers, policies and ack positions
transport acknowledgement, fn retention receipt, dregg receipt and B ack have distinct issuers/meanings
uncertain post yields one accepted Q or a definitive absence before retry
A's processing is independent of B's ack
cuts: after B ack before Q post
after B post publication before reply
after A poll before A transaction

traces.name: authorship versus application receipt and correlation
actions: deliver R with valid fn signature but false DR
deliver a reply Q2 whose Message-ID references MR but whose source correlation is wrong
deliver R3 with unknown application payload version
B and A poll through these articles and reopen
expect: authorship verdict does not make false DR valid
Q2 does not satisfy R's correlation but remains attributable evidence if admitted
R3 has no application authority and parsing stays within limits
no application transition is inferred from fn ack alone
cuts: after each consumer transaction before ack
